headline: Nvidia's board is reportedly weighing ousting Jensen Huang, knocking Nasdaq futures just after a CoreWeave-led rally lifted the Semis ETF 4.8%.
regime: Wednesday's close was a relief rally: Semis ETF +4.8%, memory +10.7% and networking +9.0% on the day after CoreWeave's beat-and-raise, but semis are still -14.2% on the month and every AI segment is down 8-27% on the month. The 10-year sits at 5.0% with the market pricing Fed hikes, and overnight Nvidia sank about 8% after hours on reports the board may remove Huang, with futures and European chips lower. Money is rotating within AI (AMD, Broadcom, power and cooling up on five days; Nvidia -13.2%) rather than leaving it, but the bounce has not yet survived a bad headline.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Power +11.4% and cooling +10.8% on five days, the best AI segments; AAON +31.0% (digest segments)
Quanta is growing faster than its March plan on power and data-centre demand (cf85d70ba4cd); Hubbell's data-centre sales rose more than 80% organically (6a3cacb3af7c)
Modine opened a new 682,000 sq ft chiller plant in Texas (ddba86653dab)
Against: Constellation's CEO still says there are 6-7 years of untapped power (36bb33e0008f); GE Vernova's Ontario SMR faces delays and cost overruns (d15f3619219d)
theses.change_note: +1: Quanta and Hubbell order data back the thesis and the tape rotated toward power and cooling while Nvidia fell; the 'untapped power' objection stands.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Rental capacity is sold out even as analysts trim buildout forecasts (f748b25e30d2)
Memory shortage is lifting Micron and Sandisk; Micron's 2027 HBM is mostly sold (ada339a28e33, 54827fb23256)
Alphabet drew $5bn of orders for an AI debt sale (2eab7e76b00d)
Against: analysts are trimming the trillion-dollar buildout (f748b25e30d2)
theses.change_note: Sold-out capacity and the memory shortage confirm yesterday's view; trimmed sell-side forecasts offset it.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave's $4bn debt plan faces an Nvidia-sized risk given its financial ties to the chipmaker (164f669ca506, e55766d207b9)
CoreWeave carries a $47bn debt load against a $133bn backlog (d7585dafb5e2)
Against: Morningstar calls the debt concerns overblown with $20bn available (cab5d5c5cb7e); segment +8.4% on five days
theses.change_note: Nvidia's leadership crisis adds a new counterparty risk, but the five-day rally and Morningstar's view balance it.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Sandisk trades at 3.4x forward earnings with an 8% FCF yield and 73% operating margin (shortlist)
Memory +10.7% on the day as the AI memory shortage lifts Micron and Sandisk (digest segments, ada339a28e33)
Against: still -3.3% on five days and -26.7% on the month, the weakest segment over a month (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +3: the biggest one-day bounce of any segment and fresh shortage reporting; one day does not reverse a month.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Alphabet is borrowing in Asian bond markets to fund AI, drawing $5bn of orders (2eab7e76b00d)
Hyperscalers are projected to spend $1.3tn on capex in 2027 (prior worldview)
Against: hyperscalers held up best in the month (-8.0%) (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +1: a cash-rich hyperscaler issuing debt for AI is a sign capex exceeds internal cash flow.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: The 10-year is at 5.0% and gold fell below $4,000 on Fed-hike bets (digest tape, 79b4aa325214)
A strategist warns not to take the bait on a 'violent bounce' in tech (3130f1f48bc3); Bitcoin ETFs bled $1.4bn in five days (15eebd2f2fc0)
Against: the Semis ETF rose 4.8% in a day and VIX is down 35% on five days (digest tape)
theses.change_note: +1: the 10-year reached 5% and one Nvidia headline erased the bounce in futures, which is how crowded trades behave.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Moratorium fears hit Dell, Credo and Lumentum last week (prior worldview)
Against: no new policy news today, and power (+11.4%) and grid (+3.7%) rose on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -2: nothing new on moratoria and the most exposed segments rallied; the risk stays but is not building.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Nvidia's board reportedly met to decide Huang's fate and weighs an interim CEO; shares fell about 8% after hours (207b754f10a0, aeab6168ec7c, 653e629ff262)
Dan Ives values Nvidia at $225 without Huang versus $300 with him (e8399f502a10)
AMD and Broadcom rallied premarket as funds rotated out of Nvidia (b32b18dcf733, c7fbc00a5b36)
theses.change_note: +15: the key-person risk is now an active board process, not a probe; the contagion runs through CoreWeave and Nvidia's financing ties.

compute.note: AMD +13.1% and NVDA -13.2% on five days; Huang's possible ouster helps rivals as much as it hurts Nvidia.

foundry_equipment.note: +7.0% on five days led by ONTO; still -19.8% on the month with fat margins.

memory_storage.note: +10.7% in a day on the shortage, but -26.7% on the month; wait for the bounce to hold.

networking_optical.note: +6.5% on five days, COHR +20.2%; Cisco's print is the next demand test.

servers.note: -26.9% on the month; Dell and Super Micro tumbled on Nvidia ties and moratorium fears.

power_nuclear.note: +11.4% on five days, the best segment; Constellation's Q3 beat and new Peak+ contracts.

grid_electrical.note: Quanta ahead of plan and Hubbell data-centre sales +80%; +3.7% on five days.

cooling_thermal.note: +10.8% on five days, AAON +31%; Modine's new Texas chiller plant is live.

datacenter_neocloud.note: +8.4% on five days, but CoreWeave's debt now carries Nvidia counterparty risk.

hyperscalers.note: -0.2% on five days; Alphabet funding AI with debt.

ai_software.note: -21.9% on the month; only ETF flows into Palantir in the news.

risks: A disorderly Nvidia CEO change could spread to CoreWeave, Dell, Super Micro and every name tied to Nvidia's financing.
Friday's PPI could push the 10-year above 5% and harden December hike bets.
A Texas or federal data-centre moratorium would hit grid, cooling, power and servers at once.
A weak Anthropic IPO would remove what analysts call the core driver of the AI trade.
If power is less scarce than assumed (Constellation's view), power and grid premiums compress.
watch: The Nvidia board's decision on Huang and the stock's reaction at the open.
Whether power, grid and cooling hold up if Nvidia sells off again (test of the rotation).
Cisco's earnings for AI networking demand and Nebius's Q3 report.
Any Texas legislative move on data-centre moratoria.
